commitment.title: The commitment (read before joining)
items: 48h setup: join the round's Google Group and opt in to every other dev's app on the Play Store.
14 days: open all 12 apps, each on at least 2 distinct days, and check in here.
3 written feedbacks (≥ 80 characters) during the round. No one tests their own app.
commitment.foot: ~15 min per day. No-shows sink the round for 12 people — that's why we say it upfront.

items.a: No. Dozena is open source (AGPL-3.0) and free during the MVP. You pay nothing: you test other devs' apps in your round and they test yours — it's a swap, not a service.

items.q: Does this guarantee Google Play approval?
items.a: No — and nobody can (services claiming a '100% guarantee' are offering a refund, not approval). Dozena organizes the tester swap so you meet the 12 testers / 14 days rule; the final decision is always Google's.
The other developers in your round — at least 12. All of them are devs with their own app in the same situation, starting in the same window. Nobody tests their own app.

items.q: What exactly do I have to do?
items.a: 4 things: (1) register your app with your closed-testing opt-in link and your Google Group; (2) during the 48h setup, join the group and opt in to everyone else's apps; (3) for 14 days, open the 12 apps on at least 2 distinct days and check in; (4) write short feedback (≥ 80 characters) on 3 apps. About 15 min per day.

items.q: What if someone drops out mid-round?
items.a: Rounds start with headroom (13–16 devs for a minimum of 12 testers per app) and every participant has a public reliability ranking — quitters lose priority in future rounds. Since everyone needs the same 14-day window, dropout rates are far lower than in loose swap groups.

items.q: How is this different from Reddit/Telegram swap groups?
items.a: Those are manual and scattered: everyone starts on a different day, nobody tracks anything, and most people quit by day 3. Here the round is synchronized (everyone starts together), check-ins prove real usage on distinct days, and reputation is public.
